note: City services of the example city. Procedures, fees and timing are original samples, not the rules of any real city; `sections` are real sections of the published code; `sources` name the real public pages read while writing each sample (see sources.json).

services.name: Residential building permit
services.summary: Permit to build, add on to, or remodel a home or accessory building.

fields.label: Type of work
fields.hint: new home, addition, remodel, garage, shed, deck

fields.label: Contractor name and license number
fields.hint: or 'owner-builder'

fields.label: Are plans ready?
fields.hint: yes or no

procedure: Planning & Zoning checks the project against the zoning rules first.
Submit the application with a site plan and building plans.
The Building Official reviews the plans and may ask for changes.
Pay the permit fee, then post the permit at the job site.
Call for each required inspection before covering the work.
services.timing: Plan review usually takes about 10 working days for a complete residential submittal.
services.fees: Permit fees are based on the value of the work; see the fee schedule.
review_points: Zoning compliance has been checked by Planning & Zoning.
A site plan shows the structure and its distances from property lines.
Building plans are complete enough to review.
The contractor's license is on file, or the owner is building the work.

services.name: Building inspection request
services.summary: Schedule an inspection for work under an open building permit.

fields.label: Type of inspection
fields.hint: footing, foundation, framing, rough plumbing, rough electrical, insulation, final

procedure: Request the inspection at least one working day ahead.
Keep the approved plans and permit card on site.
Leave the work uncovered until it has been inspected.
The inspector leaves a result; any correction needs a re-inspection.
services.timing: Requests received by 3 p.m. are usually scheduled for the next working day.
review_points: The permit number matches an open permit.
The inspection type is the next one due.
The requested date gives at least one working day of notice.

services.name: Demolition permit
services.summary: Permit to tear down a building or structure.

fields.label: Are utilities disconnected?
fields.hint: water, sewer, gas, power

procedure: Have every utility shut off and capped by the utility provider.
Have older buildings checked for asbestos before work starts.
Submit the application and pay the fee.
Haul debris to an approved site; burning it on site is not an option.
Call for a final inspection when the lot is cleared.
services.timing: Review usually takes about 5 working days.
review_points: Utility disconnections are confirmed.
An asbestos check is on file for older buildings.
A debris disposal site is named.

services.name: Start or stop utility service
services.summary: Start, transfer or stop water, sewer and trash service at an address.

fields.label: Forwarding address for the final bill

procedure: Give at least two working days' notice.
Provide photo identification; renters also show a lease.
Staff read the meter on the start or stop date.
The first or final bill is sent to the address on the account.
services.timing: Service usually starts or stops within two working days.
services.fees: Deposits and reconnect charges come from the fee schedule.
review_points: No delinquent debt to the city is on the applicant's record.
Proof of identity and of occupancy is on file.
The date gives enough notice.

services.name: Utility billing question
services.summary: A question about a bill, a late charge, a high bill or a payment.

fields.label: Account number
fields.hint: if known

procedure: Billing staff pull the account and meter reads.
A high bill is checked against past use, and a re-read of the meter can be requested.
If a leak is the cause, staff explain the sample leak adjustment: a repaired leak may qualify for a one-time credit with a plumber's receipt.
Staff write back with what they found.
services.timing: Staff usually answer within 3 working days.
review_points: The account matches the service address.
Recent meter reads were compared with past use.
If a leak is claimed, proof of repair is on file.

services.name: Report a utility outage or water leak
services.summary: Report no water, low pressure, a broken main, or a sewer backup. Gas smells are a 911 call.

fields.label: Location
fields.hint: the map pin or the closest address

fields.label: What is happening?
fields.hint: no water, low pressure, leak, sewer backup

procedure: The report goes to the on-call crew.
A crew checks the main and the meter.
If the problem is on the private side of the meter, staff say so and a plumber is needed.
Staff post a notice if a repair will shut off water for an area.
services.timing: The crew usually responds the same day.
review_points: The location can be found from the pin or address.
The kind of problem is clear.
Anything urgent was passed to the on-call crew.

services.name: Hydrant flow test request
services.summary: Ask the city to test the flow and pressure at a fire hydrant, usually for sprinkler design.

fields.label: Location
fields.hint: the hydrant nearest the site

fields.label: Why the test is needed
fields.hint: for example sprinkler design

procedure: Only city crews open a hydrant; no one else may operate one.
Staff pick the test and flow hydrants and schedule a date.
Crews run the test and record static, residual and flow readings.
The results are sent in writing.
services.timing: Tests are usually scheduled within 10 working days, outside peak water use.
services.fees: A test fee comes from the fee schedule.
review_points: The test and flow hydrants are identified.
The purpose is stated.
The date avoids peak water use and any water restriction.

services.name: Report a pothole or road hazard
services.summary: Report a pothole, road damage, debris, a missing sign or another hazard in the street. Use the map to mark the spot.

fields.label: Location
fields.hint: the map pin or the closest address

fields.label: What is the hazard?
fields.hint: pothole, debris, missing sign, damaged sidewalk

fields.label: Size or how bad it is

procedure: The report goes on the crew's work list.
A crew lead looks at the spot and ranks it by safety.
Dangerous hazards are marked or blocked first.
Repairs are scheduled by priority and weather.
services.timing: Staff usually inspect within 2 working days.
review_points: The spot is on a city street, not a state highway or private road.
The hazard is clear enough for a crew to find.
Anything dangerous has been flagged.

services.name: Report a street light out
services.summary: Report a street light that is out, flickering or damaged.

fields.label: Location
fields.hint: the map pin or the closest address

fields.label: Pole number, if you can see it
What is wrong?
fields.hint: out, flickering, on all day, damaged

procedure: Staff confirm who owns the pole.
City lights go on the repair list; lights owned by the power company are passed to it.
services.timing: Repairs usually take 5 to 10 working days.
review_points: The pole can be identified.
It is known who owns the light.

services.name: Report a storm drain problem
services.summary: Report a blocked storm drain, standing water, or something being dumped into a drain.

fields.label: Location
fields.hint: the map pin or the closest address

fields.label: What is happening?
fields.hint: blocked, flooding, dumping

procedure: A crew checks the drain and clears it if needed.
Dumping reports are shared with Code Enforcement.
services.timing: Staff usually inspect within 2 working days, sooner during storms.
review_points: The drain can be found from the pin.
Any dumping was passed to Code Enforcement.

services.name: Excavation permit (work in the street)
services.summary: Permit to dig in a public street, sidewalk or easement.

fields.label: Location
fields.hint: where the digging will happen

fields.label: Size of the excavation
fields.hint: length, width and depth

fields.label: Traffic control plan?
fields.hint: yes or no

procedure: Submit the written, signed application with the size and purpose of the work.
Show proof of insurance and a traffic control plan.
Call 811 to have utilities marked before digging.
Keep safe passage and proper signs in place while working.
Call for an inspection before backfilling and paving.
services.timing: Review usually takes about 5 working days.
services.fees: A permit fee and any deposit come from the fee schedule.
review_points: The application is written and signed, with the size of the excavation.
A traffic control plan follows the signing standard the code names.
Insurance is on file.

services.name: Non-emergency police report
services.summary: Report something that already happened, with no danger now and no known suspect: lost property, minor theft, vandalism.

fields.label: Do you know who did it?
fields.hint: if yes, an officer needs to talk with you

procedure: This form is for past events with no danger now. Anything happening right now is a 911 call.
An officer reads the report and may call you.
A report with a known suspect, or a crime against a person, is handled by an officer in person.
You get a report number once it is accepted.
services.timing: An officer usually reviews reports within 3 working days.
review_points: The event is in the past with no danger now.
It happened inside the city.
No known suspect or crime against a person means this form fits; otherwise an officer follows up.

services.name: Police records request
services.summary: Ask for a copy of a police report or another police record.

fields.label: Your connection to the case
fields.hint: for example involved party, attorney, insurer

procedure: Describe the record clearly enough for staff to find it.
Show identification when you pick up the record.
Staff review the record under the state's records law; parts may be withheld.
If the request is denied, the letter explains how to appeal.
services.timing: State law generally gives a government office up to 10 working days to respond.
services.fees: Copy costs come from the fee schedule.
review_points: The record is described clearly.
The requester's connection to the case is stated.
Any part withheld is identified under the records law.

services.name: Police standby for an event
services.summary: Ask for officers to be on site at a private or community event.

fields.label: Why officers are needed
fields.hint: for example crowd, traffic, money handling

procedure: Apply at least 14 days before the event.
The Chief decides how many officers are needed, or whether any are available.
The event host pays for officer time at the posted rate.
A parade or anything on a street also needs a city permit.
Officers follow police rules at all times, not the host's instructions.
services.timing: Apply at least 14 days ahead; staff usually answer within 5 working days.
services.fees: Officers are billed by the hour with a sample minimum of 3 hours; see the fee schedule.
review_points: The request arrived at least 14 days ahead.
Attendance, alcohol and hours are stated.
Any needed event or parade permit is noted.
Officer availability has been checked.

services.name: House watch while you are away
services.summary: Ask officers to check on your home while you are out of town.

fields.label: Who else may be at the home?
Lights or vehicles left on or parked

procedure: Officers drive by or walk around as patrol time allows.
A check is not a guarantee of protection.
Tell the department if you come home early.
services.timing: Requests should arrive at least 2 days before you leave. Sample limit: 30 days.
review_points: The dates are clear and within the limit.
An emergency contact is listed.

services.name: Fire alarm inspection request
services.summary: Schedule a fire department inspection of a fire alarm system: new, changed or annual.

fields.label: Type of inspection
fields.hint: new system, change to a system, annual

procedure: New or changed systems need approved plans before work starts.
The alarm contractor tests the system first.
A technician must be present for the inspection.
The Fire Marshal witnesses the test and records the result.
Tell the monitoring company before a test so no false alarm is sent.
services.timing: Inspections are usually scheduled within 5 working days.
services.fees: An inspection fee comes from the fee schedule. False alarm charges are set under section 131-3.
review_points: The building and system are identified.
A technician will be on site.
Plans are on file for a new or changed system.
The monitoring company has been told.

services.name: Open burn permit
services.summary: Permit for an open burn such as a weed or brush pile.

fields.label: What will be burned?
fields.hint: for example yard waste, ditch weeds

procedure: Only clean yard and ditch waste may be burned: no trash, tires, or construction waste.
Check the burn day status before lighting; burning stops on days with poor air or high wind.
An adult stays with the fire with water or tools at hand until it is fully out.
Sample seasons: state rules generally close open burning for part of the year, so ask about current dates.
The department can cancel a permit at any time.
services.timing: Staff usually answer within 2 working days and may visit the site first.
review_points: The material is allowed to be burned.
The date is in an open burn period.
Distances from buildings and fences are safe.
Water or tools will be on hand.

services.name: Fire records or information request
services.summary: Ask for a fire incident report, inspection record, or information such as response times.

fields.label: What you want
fields.hint: for example a fire incident report, response times

procedure: Describe the record or data you want.
Staff pull it from department records.
Records are reviewed under the state's records law; medical details are withheld.
Trust City has no real response data: any figures here would be samples.
services.timing: State law generally gives a government office up to 10 working days to respond.
services.fees: Copy costs come from the fee schedule.
review_points: The record or data is described clearly.
Private or medical details are withheld.

services.name: Fireworks display permit
services.summary: Permit for a public fireworks show run by a licensed operator.

fields.label: Licensed operator name and license number

procedure: Apply at least 30 days before the show.
Only a state-licensed display operator may run it.
Show proof of insurance naming the city.
The Fire Marshal inspects the site and the set-up.
Fire restrictions can cancel a permit.
services.timing: Apply at least 30 days ahead.
services.fees: A permit fee comes from the fee schedule.
review_points: The operator's license is on file.
Insurance is on file.
The site and safe distances have been reviewed.
No fire restriction is in effect.

services.name: Park pavilion reservation
services.summary: Reserve a park pavilion or field for a party, reunion or group.

fields.label: Will there be amplified music, bounce houses or vendors?

procedure: Reservations are first come, first served.
A deposit holds the date and is returned if the site is left clean.
Cancel at least 14 days ahead for a refund.
Parks close at dark unless the city gives a permit to stay.
Large groups or events open to the public may need a special event permit.
services.timing: Staff usually confirm within 3 working days.
services.fees: Sample rates: $40 for a half day, plus a $50 refundable deposit. Residents pay less than non-residents at many cities.
review_points: The date is open.
The group size fits the pavilion.
The hours end by dark or a permit is requested.
Extras are noted, and a special event permit is flagged if needed.

services.name: Special event permit
services.decider: The City Manager's designee, with Police, Fire and Public Works
services.summary: Permit for a festival, race, parade, market or other event on public property.
procedure: Apply at least 45 days before the event.
Police, Fire, Public Works and Parks each review it.
A site map or route is required.
Larger events need insurance naming the city.
Food vendors need their own health and business approvals.
services.timing: Apply at least 45 days ahead.
services.fees: An application fee and any city service costs come from the fee schedule.
review_points: A site map or route is attached.
Each department has reviewed it.
Insurance is on file.
Parade, street or vendor rules are covered.

services.name: Recreation program sign-up
services.summary: Sign someone up for a city recreation program or ask about one.
procedure: Sign up before the deadline for the program.
A parent or guardian signs for anyone under 18.
Refunds are given before a program starts, minus a small processing charge.
services.timing: Staff usually confirm within 3 working days.
services.fees: Program fees vary; sample programs run $25 to $60.
review_points: The program has space.
The age fits the program.
A guardian signed for anyone under 18.

services.name: Code complaint
services.summary: Report weeds, junk, a nuisance or other property conditions.

fields.label: How long has it been going on?

procedure: The officer reads the report and checks the site.
Reports are described as what was seen; only the officer finds whether a violation exists.
If there is one, the owner gets a notice and a chance to fix it first.
Your report is a government record; ask staff how the records law treats your name.
services.timing: An officer usually checks the site within 5 working days.
review_points: The property is identified.
The condition is described as it was seen.
The section that may apply is named.
A site visit is scheduled.

services.name: Animal complaint
services.summary: Report a barking dog, a loose animal or another animal problem. A dangerous animal on the loose is a 911 call.
procedure: The officer reads the report and may visit.
For barking, the code sets a measure of how long and how often: keep a dated log.
The owner usually gets a warning first.
A bite goes to the officer the same day.
services.timing: An officer usually responds within 2 working days.
review_points: The address and animal are identified.
Dates and times are given.
Any bite was handled the same day.

services.name: Dog license
services.summary: License a dog in the city.
procedure: Bring proof of rabies vaccination.
Pay the license fee.
Put the tag on the dog's collar.
services.timing: Licenses are usually issued the same day.
services.fees: Fees are set under section 90-34 and the fee schedule.
review_points: A vaccination certificate is on file.
The dog is old enough to need a license.
The fee is paid.

services.name: Public records request
services.summary: Ask for a copy of a city record under the state's records law.

fields.label: Records you want
fields.hint: describe them as exactly as you can

procedure: A written request names the records with reasonable detail.
The Recorder finds the record and reviews it under the records law.
You get the record, or a letter saying what is withheld and why.
A denial can be appealed; section 5-5 explains how.
services.timing: State law generally gives a government office up to 10 working days to respond, and less for some urgent requests.
services.fees: Costs are set under section 5-2 and the fee schedule.
review_points: The request describes the record reasonably.
The requester's name and address are present.
Any denial explains the appeal right.

services.name: Business license
services.summary: License a business in the city, including a business at home.

fields.label: State tax ID, if you have one

procedure: Register the business with the state first.
Planning & Zoning checks that the use fits the zone; a home business has its own rules.
Fire and Building may inspect the space.
The City Manager or designee approves the license.
Licenses are renewed each year.
services.timing: Review usually takes about 10 working days.
services.fees: Fees are set under section 110-5 and the fee schedule.
review_points: Zoning has been checked.
State registration is on file.
Inspections are noted.

services.name: Meeting agenda or minutes request
services.summary: Find a City Council meeting, agenda or minutes, or ask to speak at a meeting.

fields.label: What do you need?
fields.hint: agenda, minutes, recording, a spot to speak

procedure: State law requires public notice of each meeting and its agenda.
Agendas are posted before each meeting and on the state's public notice website.
Approved minutes are kept by the Recorder.
To speak, ask the Recorder to be added to the agenda.
services.timing: Agendas are posted at least 24 hours before a meeting.
review_points: The meeting is identified.
The request is sent to the right body.
